runs.text: Instruction Fine-Tuning datasets are critical; small, high-quality, and diverse datasets can rival larger corpora.
Multilingual models often fail in low-resource languages, making dataset construction the upper bound for their capabilities.
The Superficial Alignment Hypothesis posits fine-tuning only aligns style, but its multilingual validity remains unverified.
Key challenges include the lack of extensible quality scoring, English-centric diversity studies, and unverified multilingual SAH.
We propose M-DaQ, a diversity-driven retrieval method to improve multilinguality and mitigate data skewness across 18 languages.
